messages.content: 你能給我從舊金山家裡到帕羅奧圖辦公室最快的路線，然後從帕羅奧圖到舊金山金門大橋的風景路線，最後從金門大橋回家最快的路線嗎？

function.name: get_directions
function.description: Retrieve directions from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting point of the journey.

end_location.description: The destination point of the journey.

route_type.description: Type of route to use (e.g., fastest, scenic). Default is fastest.

message.reasoning: The user wants directions from home to Palo Alto office, then from Palo Alto to Golden Gate Bridge scenic route, then from Golden Gate Bridge back home fastest route. We need to call get_directions twice: first from home to Palo Alto, second from Palo Alto to Golden Gate Bridge. The third leg is from Golden Gate Bridge to home. But we only have two legs? Actually we need three legs: home->Palo Alto, Palo Alto->Golden Gate Bridge, Golden Gate Bridge->home. We can call get_directions twice? The user wants all three legs. We can call get_directions twice: first home->Palo Alto, second Palo Alto->Golden Gate Bridge. Then we can compute Golden Gate Bridge->home manually? But we don't have a function for that. We can call get_directions again for Golden Gate Bridge->home. So we need to call get_directions three times. The user didn't specify route_type for the first and third legs, so default fastest. For second leg scenic. So we need to call get_directions with start_location "home", end_location "Palo Alto office". Then second call start_location "Palo Alto office", end_location "Golden Gate Bridge", route_type "scenic". Third call start_location "Golden Gate Bridge", end_location "home". We need to provide the function calls.
